steps.title: Key Shift
steps.body: Move from describing ("This shows Macbeth is ambitious") to analysing ("Shakespeare presents ambition as destructive through the metaphor of...").

steps.title: Always ask
steps.body: HOW does the writer create this effect? Never just state WHAT happens - explain HOW it's achieved through language, form, and structure.

steps.title: Top Tip
steps.body: A Grade 9 critical style is invisible — the examiner does not notice your language because it sounds authoritative and effortless. The quickest way to lose marks is to write informally or to describe the plot. Before the exam, memorise 5-7 analytical verbs (presents, implies, conveys, subverts, reinforces, emphasises, challenges) and commit to never using "shows" or "uses" again.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: What's the difference between describing and analysing? | Give three examples of analytical verbs. | What does AO1 require about personal response?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Describing: telling what happens ("Macbeth kills Duncan"). Analysing: explaining HOW and WHY the writer presents it ("Shakespeare uses the motif of blood to show Macbeth's guilt after the murder"). | Analytical verbs: presents, portrays, depicts, suggests, implies, highlights, emphasises, conveys, reinforces, contrasts (any three). | AO1 requires an "informed personal response" - your interpretation supported by evidence, evaluating the writer's methods and their effects.
